title: Zero-term homology and canonical cycle maps of a short complex
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian]. Let $S=(X_1\xrightarrow{f}X_2\xrightarrow{g}X_3)$ be a short complex, meaning $g\circ f=0$. Write $Z=\ker g$, let $i:Z\to X_2$ be its kernel inclusion, let $\widetilde f:X_1\to Z$ be the unique factorization of $f$, and put $H(S)=\operatorname{coker}\widetilde f$, with quotient map $\pi:Z\to H(S)$. If $X_2$ is a zero object, then $H(S)$ is a zero object. If $g=0$, then $i$ is an isomorphism. If $f=0$, then $\pi$ is an isomorphism.
